answer: Each agent registers via a trusted execution environment attesting to a physically unclonable function in its CPU package; the identity credential is bound to that chip and cannot move. A sybil attacker must buy one separate processor and lock one stake per fake identity, so flooding the network costs linear hardware plus collateral for every duplicate. This closes the cheap inlet for fake accounts because software copies cannot reproduce the silicon secret, leaving each agent an island of attested hardware rather than an ivory-tower pseudonym.
